_README: Published cumulative-ascent figures to check lib/elevation_gain.py's dead
`sections` is EMPTY ON PURPOSE and the check fails while it stays that
way. Inventing plausible-looking section figures would make an
unvalidated threshold look validated, which is worse than no check: the
whole reason this file exists is that a gain number can agree with a
consensus by construction and mean nothing. An empty table that fails
To fill it in: pick sections with a well-known, quotable gain figure and
unambiguous mileposts - the Whites (Franconia Ridge, the Presidentials),
the Roan Highlands, the Blood Mountain climb - and record where each
number came from. Two or three sections of genuinely different character
are worth more than a dozen from the same guidebook, because the point is
that ONE threshold has to work for all of them.
Mileposts are northbound miles from Springer, matching
elevation_profile.json's distance_mi. Note that AT mileages shift between
years as the trail is relocated, so `source_year` is not optional detail.

sections.name: human-readable, e.g. 'Franconia Ridge'
sections.tolerance: optional: overrides check_elevation_gain.SECTION_TOLERANCE for this section
sections.tolerance_reason: REQUIRED when tolerance is overridden - the check refuses a silent widening

_mileposts: start_mi/end_mi are on the calibrated NOBO axis (#652) - ATC's own
half-mile Measure scale, which elevation_profile.json's distance_mi has
used since PR #765. Each anchor below was located by projecting a known
trailhead/summit coordinate onto that axis (the `_anchor` notes record
the residual - how far the coordinate sat from the centerline). Re-derive
any of them with export_elevation.calibrated_trail_axis and a Point;

whole_trail.source: commonly cited consensus figure for the full AT, as recorded in issue #91
_note: Approximate and rounded, and treated as such. It is reported by
check_elevation_gain.py but never gates: one scalar against one free
parameter is not a test, because some threshold always hits it.

sections.name: Katahdin via the Hunt Trail
sections.source: Baxter State Park's Hunt Trail figure (5.2 mi one-way, 4,188 ft), as republished by Bangor Daily News and NortheastHikes
_anchor: Katahdin Stream Campground (45.8875, -68.9994) projects to mile
2192.54 (9 m off the centerline); Baxter Peak (45.9044, -68.9214) to
2197.86 = the axis top (10 m off). The Hunt Trail IS the A.T. here,
one-way ascent, so the published walk and this window are the same
miles by construction. Character: sustained alpine climb - barely
exercises the dead band, anchors the top of the scale.

sections.name: Moosilauke via the Glencliff Trail
sections.source: AllTrails route 'Mount Moosilauke via Glencliff Trail and Appalachian Trail' (7.8 mi round trip, 3,333 ft gain; GPS/DEM-derived route stats)
_anchor: (43 m off the centerline); the start is the summit minus the cited
3.9-mile one-way length. The Glencliff Trail is the A.T.'s NOBO
ascent. Weakest source of the three - route-stat aggregation, not a
land manager - kept because a second sustained climb in a different
range, on different DEM projects, is still worth a row. Character:

sections.name: Carvers Gap to US 19E (Roan Highlands)
sections.source: TEHCC (the section's maintaining club), trail wiki 'Carver's Gap to US19E': 14.8 mi, 2,054 ft gain / 4,703 ft loss, stated south-to-north
tolerance_reason: Cumulative gain on rolling, descent-dominated terrain is
methodology-dependent, and the honest published sources disagree with
a dense DEM sum by more than the default 10% of this section's small
denominator. Measured 2026-08-18 against the calibrated-axis profile:
our 3 m figure is 2,441 ft (+18.8% vs TEHCC's 2,054; AllTrails'
route stat is 2,145); the window contains zero part boundaries and
zero physically-impossible steps, its extra feet sit exactly where
the named climbs are (Round Bald, Little Hump, Hump Mountain) plus
~400 ft of small real rolls dense sampling counts and smoothed
sources do not; and NO threshold in the 0-10 m sweep brings it
within 10% of TEHCC (10 m still reads +12.4%) while the same
thresholds sit within +/-4% on both pure ascents above. Tuning the
dead band to this section would trade agreement with a known-meaning
figure for agreement with an unknown smoothing. 25% still catches
the failure class this file exists for - the 17% systematic
over-count arrived ON TOP of an honest baseline, and a recurrence
lands this section near +40%. Character: rolling descent-heavy
balds - the discriminating case for the dead band.
